note: Ten stories. Several UK items rest on a single secondary outlet because BBC, Guardian, Sky, Reuters and FT pages could not be opened; those stories say so. No confirmation of the electric car target decision was found, so it is left out.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia as chief executive; CFO Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis
stories.standfirst: Sources differ on whether the board ousted him or he resigned, days after Nvidia opened an independent inquiry into him.
body: Huang ceased to be Nvidia's chief executive on Thursday 12 November. Bloomberg, carried by Claims Journal, says the board ousted him after reports of two relationships, one with a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore data-centre firm suspected of spying for China. TechCrunch says he resigned. CFO Colette Kress is interim chief executive, and the board named Harvey Jones, 73, who previously led Synopsys, as its first chair.

Bloomberg reports the shares fell more than 10 per cent in premarket trading and that Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon downgraded the stock to market-perform with a $200 target. Wachtell's Joon H. Kim is running the independent investigation announced earlier this week, and lawmakers have threatened a subpoena. Megaspeed is under US investigation over alleged chip smuggling; Nvidia and Megaspeed both deny wrongdoing.

TechCrunch reports on the effect on open-source AI. Huang championed the Nemotron open-weight family, which was expanded last month, and led a July open letter signed by 25 firms against over-restricting open-weight models. Nvidia's planned acquisition of Hugging Face, put at $12.9bn by one TechCrunch writer and $13bn by another, is scheduled to close in the first half of 2027, and Reuters reported in October that the Justice Department was asking about its competitive impact. Hugging Face's chief executive has said he will keep fighting for open-source AI. Saxo's morning note lists Nvidia's earnings for 17 November.

sources.name: TechCrunch, Huang's exit and open source

stories.headline: Putin meets Witkoff and Kushner; prisoner exchange 'finalised' but no numbers published
stories.standfirst: The US envoys flew from Abu Dhabi to Moscow and then to Dublin to brief Zelensky; Europe is to join the next round.
body: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin on 12 November, after the two-day Abu Dhabi talks. RFE/RL puts the meeting at about two and a half hours and Witkoff's tenth with Putin. Witkoff said progress had been made and a new meeting set, and that European representatives would join the next trilateral round. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov, quoted by Reuters, called the talks useful, said direct talks with Kyiv would continue and said Putin would discuss Ukraine with Donald Trump at the APEC summit in China later this month.

On territory nothing has moved. Reuters describes the talks as deadlocked, with the Kremlin still demanding all of Donbas and Kyiv refusing. Putin proposed a joint humanitarian mission to Kostiantynivka, modelled on the Oleshky evacuation; Russia says it needs five days to clear mines and Reuters says the US side backed it. Kyiv's presidential office says Russia used the Oleshky operation to move equipment and rotate troops and wants details.

Kushner and Witkoff then met Volodymyr Zelensky for just under an hour at Baldonnel Aerodrome near Dublin, on the edge of the European Political Community summit. Kushner said the prisoner deal was finalised and that the US could not conclude a deal without the Europeans at the table. Zelensky called it a real result for families. Neither side has given a number or date; TASS cites a Russian general saying more than 1,000 each, which the Kyiv Independent says is unverified, and Reuters expects it within weeks. Taoiseach Micheal Martin said no decision has been made on who represents Europe. A UK, France and Germany meeting is due in Berlin next week.

stories.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast agentic tier, and puts it behind Search
stories.standfirst: Google claims it beats Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index while running about 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash.
body: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is a low-cost, fast tier aimed at agentic work, sitting below Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon, which remain the deep-reasoning models. Google's claims, none independently checked in the sources read: about 2.5 times faster on tasks than Gemini 3.8 Flash, a higher score than Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at the default high thinking level, and fifth place on Agent Arena's multi-step benchmarks covering deep research, data analysis and codebase navigation.

There are four thinking levels: low, medium, high (the default) and a new xhigh. Google says Hydrogen can run everyday coding loops on its own, writing code, running tests and verifying, or sit in multi-model workflows with Carbon and Argon.

It is rolling out to all Search users globally, where Google describes a stronger fan-out that splits a query into subqueries, better instruction following and tool calling, and more structured AI Mode output such as tables and custom tools. It is available in all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and the Gemini app, and in Antigravity for paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers only.

TechCrunch's report gives no price per million tokens, context length, parameter count or exact benchmark scores. The aggregator Opper lists it on 12 November with an intelligence score of 54 and no price or context length.

stories.headline: wfx-loot: 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts used to plant a CI secret stealer
stories.standfirst: The campaign, named by Aikido, began on Tuesday and leaves persistence that survives secret rotation.
body: Aikido says each compromised account opens a probe pull request titled docs: dependency audit notes from a branch called wfx-docs to test write access; 61,764 repositories were probed. Where writes succeed, the account pushes a roughly 1,500-line shell stealer by injecting it into a workflow, hooking npm postinstall or adding a workflow on a throwaway branch, then reverts within about a minute and deletes the run and logs. How the credentials were stolen is not explained.

The loot includes GITHUB_TOKEN, Actions secrets, OIDC tokens, AI-tool keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor and Copilot, and AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, PyPI and SSH credential files. Self-hosted runners also lose instance metadata, Docker state and systemd units. Exfiltration is by HTTP POST to IP addresses or to a Telegram chat. Persistence survives rotation: long-lived AWS access keys, AWS role trust policies rewritten to accept any account, and wfx-ci-* federated credentials added to Azure AD apps.

Scale figures differ. Aikido counts the payload running in at least 1,806 repositories. SafeDep counts 8,093 repositories receiving malicious commits between 12:46 UTC on Tuesday and 04:36 UTC on Wednesday, with 7,309 workflow injections and 771 npm postinstall hooks. At least 50 compromised users publish packages on npm, Go, Packagist, PyPI or crates; named examples are Packagist digitalelvis/neuronai-studio 3.14.3 and Go module github.com/onuragtas/docker-env v1.0.278 and v1.0.280. Indicators include the branch name and commit titles such as ci: refresh build cache. Remediation advice is to rotate every reachable secret and remove the AWS trust-policy changes and Azure credentials. The Hacker News reported no GitHub response.

stories.headline: N-able N-central: researcher publishes further unauthenticated root exploit chains after a first batch of 33 flaws
stories.standfirst: The vendor took its hosted service offline and says it has seen scanning but no successful exploitation.
body: Researcher Sean Bales published about 33 zero-days with proofs of concept, chained into four exploits, three giving remote code execution and one root escalation, tested against N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31. N-able took Hosted N-central offline and told on-premises customers to shut servers down. Fixes landed in 2026.4 HF2 for CVE-2026-125883 (XXE), CVE-2026-125878 (OGNL injection), CVE-2026-125879 (local root via syslog-ng configuration), CVE-2026-125880 (stored XSS), CVE-2026-125881 (SSRF), CVE-2026-125882 (RCE via upload path traversal) and CVE-2026-91000 (insecure IPC leading to local privilege escalation).

On 11 November Bales published two more: 4EverAble2Shell, an unauthenticated RCE to root reportedly working against HF2 (build 2026.4.1.26), and Agent2Shell, more than ten agent and probe flaws chaining to commands as SYSTEM on managed Windows endpoints. Neither has a CVE. N-able's later advisory says the server-side chain needs the Legacy API enabled and internet-exposed, so HF2 servers with it disabled are not exposed to 4EverAble2Shell; whether Agent2Shell depends on it is unconfirmed.

N-able says it has confirmed scanning tied to the proofs of concept but no successful exploitation. watchTowr, Defused Cyber and Previdian report probing on honeypots, and Censys counts 1,728 internet-exposed instances. Huntress's guidance changed during the day, first telling customers to take even HF2 servers offline and later narrowing that to the Legacy API condition, and the two sources differ on whether hosted environments run the same build. A further hotfix is expected, and Huntress advises hunting from 8 November for rogue administrators, scheduled tasks and PowerShell or cmd launched by the agent or probe.

stories.headline: UK economy grew 0.7 per cent in the third quarter, well above expectations
stories.standfirst: Growth was almost entirely services, with computer programming at its fastest pace in three years, according to the ONS.
body: City AM, reporting the ONS figures on 12 November, says GDP rose 0.7 per cent in the third quarter after 0.6 per cent in the first and 0.5 per cent in the second. September alone grew 0.2 per cent against a forecast of no growth. Over the three months services rose 0.9 per cent and production 0.1 per cent, while construction fell 0.7 per cent.

ONS chief economist Grant Fitzner said growth was almost wholly services and that computer programming was growing at its fastest in three years, which he linked to AI-related firms. City AM adds that the Bank of England and Bloomberg Economics each attribute about a fifth of growth to AI-related investment, that spending held up despite an energy price spike linked to the Iran war, and that Lord Jim O'Neill puts annualised growth nearer 2 per cent. The OBR expects energy price effects to cut 2027 growth to 1 per cent, and NIESR forecasts 1.1 per cent. The page carries no comment from Chancellor John Healey.

For background, the Bank of England's 5 November summary shows Bank Rate raised from 3.75 to 4 per cent on an 8 to 1 vote, with Catherine Mann preferring 4.25 per cent. September CPI was 3.5 per cent, and staff project about 4.5 per cent in the first quarter of 2027 and about 5 per cent in the second. The ONS publishes October CPI on 18 November. The GDP figures here rest on one secondary outlet, as no ONS or wire page could be opened.

sources.name: Bank of England, MPC summary November 2026

stories.headline: Honda still without a root cause for Aston Martin battery failures; countermeasure needed before Las Vegas
stories.standfirst: Stroll's two separate battery problems at Interlagos were the package's third DNF across the triple-header.
body: PlanetF1 and The Race report that Lance Stroll had two separate battery problems in Brazil and did not reach mid-distance, the third retirement for the Aston Martin and Honda package across the Mexico, Sao Paulo and preceding rounds. Mexico's failure was a cooling problem inside the energy recovery system that led to MGU-K trouble, and Honda says it had not shown up in simulation.

Honda's Shintaro Orihara said the team knows what happened but not the root cause, and that the review could take a few weeks. The Race reports a countermeasure is needed before Las Vegas, with the full fix targeted for 2027, and that possible causes include part mileage or running the engine harder for performance. Troubleshooting draws on dyno hours, which the engine development rules limit, as well as staff time and cost-cap budget.

Honda's combustion engine is also still short of power, and PlanetF1 says no major step is expected at the start of 2027, with upgrades phased in through the year. Aston Martin are tenth in the constructors' championship on 7 points, all from Fernando Alonso, who reached Q3 for the first time this season in Brazil and qualified eighth with help from a chassis upgrade. Team principal Adrian Newey compared the situation with early Red Bull turmoil and said crankshaft horsepower is not the whole story.

stories.headline: 2027 grid nearly complete as Racing Bulls keep Lawson and Lindblad and Tsolov becomes reserve
stories.standfirst: Only one Cadillac seat remains open after Haas also confirmed Rafael Camara.
body: Racing Bulls will run Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad again in 2027, The Race reports. Team principal Alan Permane said the pairing balances youth and experience, and Lawson's Mexico and Brazil races reportedly helped his case. Lawson is ninth in the drivers' standings and Racing Bulls fifth among the constructors.

Nikola Tsolov misses out and becomes official reserve for both Red Bull teams in 2027, covering simulator work, Friday practice runs, testing of previous cars and tyre testing. He has six F2 wins and is a title contender with two rounds left. Haas have confirmed Camara, who leads F2 by 7 points over Tsolov, with Alex Dunne also in contention, and dropped Esteban Ocon for the rest of 2026 after an incident the article does not detail. Camara made his F1 debut at his home race in Brazil, and PlanetF1 says his Las Vegas participation is being taken one step at a time because F2 runs alongside F1 in Qatar and Abu Dhabi but not in Las Vegas.

The Race lists the 2027 line-ups as Mercedes: Antonelli and Russell; Ferrari: Leclerc and Hamilton; McLaren: Norris and Piastri; Red Bull: Verstappen and Hadjar; Racing Bulls: Lawson and Lindblad; Alpine: Gasly and Colapinto; Haas: Bearman and Camara; Audi: Hulkenberg and Bortoleto; Aston Martin: Alonso and Stroll; Williams: Albon and Sainz; Cadillac: Perez plus one seat still to be confirmed.

stories.headline: Google's Gemini Decision 1 scores closed-set answers in one forward pass at $0.10 per million input tokens
stories.standfirst: The Decisions API is a classifier-style endpoint rather than a text generator, with 150 to 250 ms latency.
body: Google's developer blog describes gemini-decision-1, which answers up to 1,000 independent questions per request by scoring closed-set options in a single forward pass rather than generating tokens. Question types are yes or no, multiple choice with 2 to 255 options, and ordered rubric scoring from 0, and every answer carries a 0 to 1 confidence score. Inputs can be text, images, audio, video and PDFs up to 256K tokens; the aggregator Opper lists 262K. The blog is dated 11 November, though some newsletters place it on 12 November.

Google states 150 to 250 ms end-to-end latency and 50 to 100 ms median compute for contexts up to 16K tokens, nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions per request. Pricing is $0.10 per million input tokens and nothing for output, with shared input billed once per request and a free tier in AI Studio. Google claims it is about five times cheaper than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite with the Interactions API on its own benchmark suite, and that it leads that suite on agent routing, reasoning, ranking and multimodal tasks with the lowest calibration error, but publishes no scores. It says Gemini Notebook saw up to 40 per cent lower latency on everyday queries using it as a router.

Access is through the google-genai SDK at v1beta. Integrations are rolling out with OpenRouter, LangChain, Vercel, LiteLLM, Pydantic AI, Pipecat, LiveKit and OpenCode, and Google Cloud support is listed as coming soon.

stories.headline: Burnham tells COP31 the UK will meet net zero by 2050, then presses for an EU deal in Dublin
stories.standfirst: He gave a short Antalya speech and met EU leaders at the European Political Community summit before next week's Brussels meeting.
body: Brit Brief reports that Andy Burnham gave a five-minute speech at COP31 in Antalya, recommitted to net zero by 2050 and appointed Dame Madeleine Alessandri as special representative for climate security. It says he was the only G7 leader addressing the summit, with the US sending no delegation, and that a planned bilateral with Brazil's President Lula was cancelled. Green Party leader Zack Polanski and Friends of the Earth's Asad Rehman criticised his domestic record, citing the reported electric car target cut, the Jackdaw gas field approval and the pending Rosebank decision.

At the European Political Community summit in Dublin, thejournal.ie's liveblog says Burnham told reporters he would fight for a good deal with the EU before the Brussels UK-EU summit on 20 November, and met Ursula von der Leyen. The liveblog says agreements on food and farming, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme are due to be signed in Brussels, a claim an earlier IBTimes page did not repeat. He also met Italy's Giorgia Meloni on the Global Combat Air Programme and co-chaired a Ukraine meeting with Volodymyr Zelensky. A draft declaration reportedly has about 40 countries backing principles of European security.

Reform's Nigel Farage and Zia Yusuf accuse Burnham of reversing a pledge not to reopen Brexit, according to IBTimes UK, while the Liberal Democrats' Monica Harding back the single market and a customs union.

today: Friday 13 November: informal meeting of EU leaders in Dublin, hosted by Micheal Martin, focused on AI.
Tuesday 17 November: Nvidia earnings; ONS labour market figures at 07:00.
Wednesday 18 November: ONS October CPI at 07:00; Anthropic IPO pricing is expected, with first trading on 19 November.
Friday 20 November: UK-EU summit in Brussels.
Las Vegas GP, UK times converted from local: first practice 00:30 Friday 20 November, qualifying 04:00 Saturday 21 November, race 04:00 Sunday 22 November.

briefs.text: Trump posted on Truth Social that the US does not need a deal with Iran, a day after the Wall Street Journal reported he had authorised Vance to lead talks; Iran's Mohsen Rezaei denies any talks are under way.

Zelensky says speed limits have returned on Starshield, the military version of Starlink, disrupting interception of Russian drones for several days; Musk says the system is controlled by the US government.

An Israeli strike hit the surgical wing of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis overnight, killing six and wounding at least a dozen according to the UN and Gaza's Health Ministry; the Israeli military says it targeted a senior Hamas militant and gave no evidence for its claim that the complex is a command centre.

Ukraine's Special Operations Forces say drones hit the Gazprom-owned Omsk refinery, about 2,500km from the border, in an eight-hour attack on 11 November; the Kyiv Independent could not verify the extent of the damage.

EU foreign ministers are expected on 16 November to sanction Wildberries chief executive Tatyana Kim and more than 40 other people and firms, with a 22nd sanctions package expected before the 26 to 27 November summit.
Toto Wolff says Mercedes could prioritise George Russell in the last three races to help him finish second in the drivers' standings, but nothing has been decided.
